newsitem.title: INDIA: Bayer nominees join India firm's board.
newsitem.headline: Bayer nominees join India firm's board.

text.p: Nominees of Bayer Industries Ltd, an wholly-owned Indian subsidiary of Bayer AG, joined the board of Indian firm ABS Industries on Tuesday, the managing director of Bayer AG's plastics business group said.
Klaus Seeger, managing director of Bayer AG's plastics business group, told Reuters he and Alan McGilvray, Bayer's India country head, joined the Indian firm's board on Tuesday.
McGilvray is the new chairman of ABS Industries and Seeger the vice-chairman.
Earlier this year, the German firm bought 51 percent of the Indian firm which manufactures acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS), a plastic resin used by the automobile and white goods industries.

Rakesh Agrawal, who continues as managing director of ABS Industries (which will be renamed Bayer ABS Ltd), said the firm's manufacturing capacity would be raised to 45,000 tonnes a year from the current 22,000 tonnes over the next two years.
The expansion will improve product quality while lowering the cost of production, Agrawal said.
"We are not going to limit ourselves to ABS," Seeger said. "ABS will be the vehicle to bring other products like polyamide and polycarbonate into India," he said.
A head start by rival GE Plastics BV of Holland saw Bayer lose its share of the Indian market for polycarbonate, an engineering plastic, industry analysts said.
Seeger said the Indian acquisition was part of Bayer's global plan to expand its position in ABS plastics.
Earlier this month, Bayer took a controlling interest in Slezinger, an ABS manufacturing unit in Brazil.
In October 1996, Bayer's Thailand subsidiary Bayer Premier Corp set up a new ABS unit. The Thai firm plans expand into the manufacture of polycarbonate, Seeger said.
"We are already serving firms such as General Motors and Whirlpool in other markets," he said, referring to the supply of ABS resin used in the manufacture of automobile and white goods.
Seeger said Bayer was exploring the possibility of establishing a manufacturing unit in China for engineering plastics such as ABS.
Bayer is studying the feasibility of building a synthetic rubber plant in India, McGilvray said.
